pois.name: Museum Fatahillah
pois.description: The centrepiece of Fatahillah Square, this 17th-century Dutch colonial building is one of the best-preserved examples of Dutch colonial architecture in Indonesia. Originally Jakarta's City Hall (Stadhuis), now a history museum.

pois.name: Pelabuhan Sunda Kelapa
pois.description: Jakarta's historic port, operational since the 12th century. Traditional two-masted wooden pinisi schooners from Sulawesi and Kalimantan still dock here, loading and unloading cargo by hand.

pois.name: Museum Bank Indonesia
pois.description: Housed in the ornate 1909 Nederlandsche Handel-Maatschappij building — one of Kota Tua's architectural gems. The museum traces Indonesia's monetary history from colonial trade to modern central banking.

pois.name: Gereja Sion
pois.description: Jakarta's oldest surviving church (1695), built by the VOC for freed Portuguese-origin slaves (called 'Mardijkers'). The interior preserves a carved mahogany pulpit and copper chandeliers from the colonial era.

pois.name: Café Batavia
pois.description: Legendary colonial-era café facing Fatahillah Square. The 200-year-old building is filled with antique photographs, gramophone horns, and memorabilia — a living museum of Old Batavia atmosphere.

pois.name: Museum Wayang
pois.description: The Puppet Museum in a 1912 colonial building. Home to over 4,000 wayang puppets from across the archipelago, from ornate Javanese wayang kulit to 3D Sundanese wayang golek.

pois.name: Museum Seni Rupa dan Keramik
pois.description: Fine Arts and Ceramics Museum occupying a colonial palace (1870) that once served as the Jakarta Supreme Court. Showcases Indonesian fine art from the 19th century to the contemporary era.

pois.name: Taman Fatahillah
pois.description: The cobblestoned central square of Kota Tua — once the largest square in Southeast Asia after Amsterdam's Dam Square. The focal point of Dutch Batavia, now a vibrant public square with street performers and café terraces.
